note: The flow-skeleton PATTERN directory -- a layer distinct from the sink/source CATALOGUE (models/) and from the kind->evaluator recipe (evaluators.json). The catalogue labels what a single node IS (this call is an alloc, this arg is a size). A PATTERN here is a structural query over the SHAPE of the taint-scoped control skeleton produced for one function -- an ordered, nesting-aware sequence of {control | sink} events. A double-free is not one node the catalogue can name; it is two `free` nodes on one path with no reallocation between them. That shape only exists at this layer. Pure data: each pattern names the skeleton alphabet it needs and the shape it matches; the engine that runs it lives outside this repo. Matches are LEADS, never verdicts.

skeleton_alphabet.note: What a rendered control skeleton puts on a line, and the per-sink facts a pattern predicates over. `emitted` marks whether the reader currently stamps that sink family onto the skeleton; a pattern requiring an un-emitted family is tier 2 (blocked) until the reader emits it.

per_sink_facts.tainted: the taint run reaches this sink's obligation value (bool)
per_sink_facts.cap: destination_capacity status: within-capacity | exceeds-capacity | capacity-known-size-unknown | unknown
per_sink_facts.dom: guard dominance: guarded-region (checked) | fall-through (guard exists, sink escapes it) | none-observed (no size guard)
per_sink_facts.line: source line -- gives flow order and nesting within the function

patterns.name: Buffer write reached around its size guard
patterns.shape: a memory.copy sink whose obligation value has dom == 'fall-through' -- a size-testing branch exists in the function but this copy is reached on the path that skips it
patterns.signal: the escaped guard is the lead; taint is a stronger corroboration, not required
patterns.note: implemented as the `missing-guard` evaluator + guard dimension (evaluators.json). Listed so the directory is complete.

patterns.name: Allocation size is attacker-influenced and unbounded
patterns.shape: a memory.alloc sink with tainted == true and cap in {exceeds-capacity, capacity-known-size-unknown}
patterns.signal: the size flows from a source and is not clamped to a bound
patterns.note: covered by the `relational` evaluator over alloc-size kinds.

patterns.name: Copy inside a loop with no bound on the iteration length
patterns.shape: a memory.copy sink nested (by brace depth / line span) under a for/while/do header, with dom != 'guarded-region' and the loop bound not derived from the destination capacity
patterns.signal: the loop can iterate past the destination; the copy is not guarded per-iteration
patterns.note: two-event shape over the control header + the copy, both already on the skeleton.

patterns.name: Allocate with one size, copy with another on the same path
patterns.shape: a memory.alloc(dst, sizeA) followed on the same path by a memory.copy(dst, src, sizeB) where sizeB is not derived from sizeA and cap != within-capacity
patterns.signal: the destination was sized for sizeA but written sizeB
patterns.note: two-node path pattern joining alloc dst to copy dst; both families emitted.

patterns.name: Free reached twice on one path (double free)
patterns.blocked_on: reader must emit memory.free lifecycle nodes
patterns.shape: two memory.free sinks on the same path over the same pointer identity with no reassignment or reallocation of that pointer between them
patterns.signal: the second free is the lead
patterns.note: canonical typestate example. Needs a memory.free constructor so free-sites land on the skeleton with a pointer identity to join on.

patterns.name: Dereference or copy of a pointer after it was freed
patterns.blocked_on: reader must emit memory.free AND memory.deref lifecycle nodes
patterns.shape: a memory.free(x) followed on the same path by a memory.deref(x) or a memory.copy reading from x, with no reassignment of x between
patterns.signal: the post-free use is the lead
patterns.note: pointer identity join is the same as double-free.

patterns.name: Address of a local returned or stored past its scope
patterns.blocked_on: reader must emit an address-of-local escape node
patterns.shape: a return (or store into an out-param / global) of the address of a stack local
patterns.signal: the escaping address is the lead
patterns.note: needs escape modeling of &local; adjacent to the deref constructor.

patterns.name: Return value dereferenced without a null/error check
patterns.blocked_on: reader must emit memory.deref nodes and mark return-value origins
patterns.shape: a call whose return is bound to r, then a memory.deref(r) on a path with no if/guard testing r between the call and the deref
patterns.signal: the unchecked deref is the lead
patterns.note: sharpened by peer-differential guard analysis once deref nodes exist.

build_order: Tier 1 runs over today's alphabet: mem.write.missing-bounds and mem.alloc.tainted-unbounded (shipped), then mem.copy.in-loop-unbounded and mem.alloc-copy.size-mismatch via a skeleton-sequence matcher.

Tier 2 unblock = two reader constructors: memory.free (free-site + pointer identity) and memory.deref (deref-site + pointer identity), plus an address-of-local escape marker. Pure structure emission, siblings of memory.alloc/copy.
Once emitted, the skeleton-sequence matcher runs the tier-2 typestate patterns (double-free, UAF, use-after-return, unchecked-return-deref).
